findings.message: Uncorroborated evidence claims with no registered or bound source: (a) the learning-styles claim "The evidence for matching teaching to a diagnosed style is weak" and its multimodal residue (docs/semester-1/efmp-301/unit-05/topic-01.mdx:96-102), directly assessed at MCQ 6 and RRQ 10; (b) the history claim "Early IQ testing was used to rank immigrants and justify exclusion, in ways the data never supported" (topic-01.mdx:118-120); (c) the prediction-strength claim "A score predicts school performance moderately well... and predicts almost nothing else a school exists to grow" (topic-01.mdx:124-126). The reviewer fetched the registered OpenStax sections 7.4 and 7.5: none of these passages appear there (7.4 has no learning-styles content; 7.5's history material is eugenics/Buck v. Bell, not immigrant ranking, and it makes no school-performance prediction statement), and the bound excerpts carry none of them. The content-spec planned supplements for exactly this material (specs/content/efmp-301/content-spec.md:672-674) but sources/unit-05.md registers none. Repair: register and bind open-access sources that carry these claims (e.g. a learning-styles evidence review; an intelligence-testing history source), or soften each claim to what bound sources support, then re-prepare the manifest and have a fresh reviewer re-verify.

Assessment blueprint deviation: the MCQ topic spread is 6/4 (unit-assessment.mdx Q1-6 -> topic 5.1, Q7-10 -> topic 5.2) and the RRQ spread is 4/6 (R1-3 and R10 -> 5.1, R4-9 -> 5.2) against the approved 5/5 for both bands (specs/content/efmp-301/content-spec.md:747-748, verified as declared by the intake-2 evaluation item 6). Topic 5.1 is over-weighted by one MCQ and topic 5.2 by one RRQ. Repair: move one MCQ from 5.1 material to 5.2 material and one RRQ from 5.2 material to 5.1 material (updating the concept graph's derived assessment IDs accordingly), or record a justified blueprint amendment in the content-spec.

The gloss on the Gardner criticism attributes more specificity than the cited source carries: "the eight intelligences do not show up as separable factors in test data" (topic-01.mdx:75-76), "the eight intelligences have not demonstrated independence in measurement" (:91-92), the teacher notes' "state the criticism's content (the eight do not separate in test data)" (unit-teacher-notes.mdx:62-63) and RRQ 2's model answer "the eight do not show as separable factors" (unit-assessment.mdx:180-181). The bound and live OpenStax text says only "heavily criticized for lacking empirical evidence" with no factor-analytic treatment. The gloss is accurate to the wider literature but uncorroborated; repair by binding a critique source that carries it or wording the gloss as the unit's own reading of "lacking empirical evidence".

The middle-positions passage names Thurstone ("Thurstone's few primary abilities, and the modern two-level accounts", topic-01.mdx:61-64) and fig-U5-1 labels "Thurstone and others: a few primary abilities", but no bound or cited source contains Thurstone (the live OpenStax 7.4 covers Spearman, Cattell, Sternberg, Gardner and CHC, not Thurstone). The position is spec-planned (content-spec.md:726-728) and historically accurate; repair by citing a source that carries it or presenting it as general history of the field.

The integrative fifth ERQ does not do what the approved blueprint describes: the spec's parenthetical (content-spec.md:750-752) calls for "a described pupil's profile read through the intelligence theories, the measurement limits and the creativity material into a justified teaching response", but ERQ 5 (unit-assessment.mdx:154-157) integrates only topic 5.2's two sub-topics (the early finisher = giftedness; the essay pupil = creativity/originality) and draws on nothing from 5.1. The teacher notes' "ERQ 5 is the capstone and integrates both topics by design" (unit-teacher-notes.mdx:105-106) overstates accordingly. Repair: widen ERQ 5 (or swap it) so the capstone genuinely reads a pupil through both topics, or amend the spec's description.

Guide-attribution overstatement: unit-teacher-notes.mdx:88-91 says "The guide's practical component for this chapter is a case study analysis" and sources/unit-05.md:24 calls it "the guide-named practical work behind the teacher notes", but the guide pairs no practical work with Chapter 5 - it lists Case Study Analysis among course-wide teaching strategies (1st 2026.txt:1173-1180) and a generic five-item Practical Work list (:1182-1189). The designed practical (each trainee brings one undersampled pupil; groups design the fifth box) is sound and uses a guide-named strategy; repair the wording to attribute it to the unit's design rather than to a chapter-specific guide component.
